disclaimer: Coordinates are geographic references, not verified entrance or observing-site coordinates. Site operation hours and gates are NOT checked live.

places.name: Headlands Dark Sky Park
places.note: County park; check event and nighttime entry rules.
places.intro: Emmet County’s lakeshore dark-sky destination, with broad horizons and a developed observatory setting.
places.whatToWatch: Lakeshore exposure can mean wind, changing nearshore cloud and chilly nights even after a warm afternoon.
places.access: Use posted park directions and the official events calendar; the map point is not an entrance.

arrival.arrival: Follow the posted signs to the dark-sky viewing area; the county park has separate trailhead and event-center parking. Grounds are available for observing 24 hours a day; no camping. Confirm any facility or event hours separately.
arrival.place: Headlands International Dark Sky Park, Mackinaw City, Michigan

places.name: Keweenaw Dark Sky Park
places.note: Keweenaw Mountain Lodge area; check overnight access.
places.intro: A dark northern-peninsula sky near Copper Harbor, surrounded by Lake Superior on three sides.
places.whatToWatch: Lake-effect clouds can obscure a sky that looks clear in a broader forecast grid. Pack for exposed, cold nights.
places.access: The Keweenaw Mountain Lodge is the documented public hub; check access and the lodge’s current programs.

arrival.arrival: Public stargazing is on the Keweenaw Mountain Lodge outdoor grounds from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m., with no camping or access to lodge buildings. The operator lists the dark-sky park CLOSED throughout April and November 15–December 14. Check the park's current calendar before travel.

places.name: Dr. T.K. Lawless County Park
places.note: County park; nighttime use may be tied to advertised hours or events.
places.intro: Southwest Michigan county park recognized for protecting its nocturnal environment.
places.whatToWatch: County-run nighttime programming and entry rules deserve as much attention as cloud cover.
places.access: Confirm announced dark-sky events and gate access before a late visit.

arrival.arrival: Cass County publishes scheduled Dark Sky Viewing dates and closing times and asks visitors to verify weather-dependent openings. Do not assume an unscheduled late-night arrival is permitted. Follow the county's posted viewing calendar.

places.name: Beaver Island Wildlife Research Area
places.note: Island sanctuary; ferry or air access and specific wildlife-area rules apply.
places.intro: International Dark Sky Sanctuary on an island in northern Lake Michigan.
places.whatToWatch: A sky forecast does not establish ferry, flight, trail, lodging or sanctuary access.
places.access: Arrange island transportation and verify wildlife-area rules; this coordinate is an area reference.

arrival.arrival: DarkSky International identifies the sanctuary lands as open 24/7, but this is an island wildlife area, not a guaranteed drive-up lookout. Arrange ferry or air travel and lodging, and obtain the sanctuary's current public-access rules before deciding on an observing point.

places.name: Lake Hudson Recreation Area
places.note: Michigan state-designated preserve; check park access.
places.intro: An inland southern Michigan state dark-sky preserve.
places.whatToWatch: Humidity, haze and scattered cloud can matter as much as artificial lighting.
places.access: Michigan’s legislatively designated preserves permit nighttime use; check park alerts and applicable vehicle rules.

arrival.arrival: Michigan DNR identifies the viewing preserve beside the park picnic shelter and says it is open 24 hours a day year-round. The park address is published, but the parking lot and any winter route are not verified live.

places.name: Negwegon State Park
places.note: Rustic park; access road not winter-plowed.
places.intro: Remote Lake Huron shoreline park in Alcona County, with a state-designated dark-sky preserve.
places.whatToWatch: The access road is not winter-plowed; do not infer vehicle access after snow.
places.access: Michigan DNR reports no winter plowing. Confirm safe, legal access before a night visit.

arrival.arrival: Michigan DNR identifies the main parking area off Sand Hill Trail; campsites are hike-in and not substitutes for a drive-up observing area. The park road is NOT plowed in winter; check the approach and legal access before traveling.

places.name: Port Crescent State Park
places.note: Dark-sky preserve section; no winter plowing; walk from parking.
places.intro: Lake Huron’s Thumb shoreline provides broad sky views from designated preserve areas.
places.whatToWatch: Onshore clouds, wind and beach conditions can change quickly.
places.access: Michigan DNR warns that the preserve is not winter-plowed; visitors may need to walk from parking.

arrival.arrival: Michigan DNR identifies the viewing platform near Parking Lot D as its best dark-sky viewing location. The day-use area and campground have SEPARATE entrances about two miles apart. The dark-sky preserve is NOT winter-plowed; walking from parking may be necessary.
arrival.place: Port Crescent State Park Parking Lot D, Michigan

places.name: Rockport Recreation Area
places.note: State preserve; winter access road is plowed.
places.intro: A state-designated northern Lake Huron preserve in a rugged former quarry landscape.
places.whatToWatch: Rugged terrain remains hazardous after sunset; stay on authorized routes.
places.access: Michigan DNR reports winter plowing; this is not a live road-condition report.

arrival.arrival: Michigan DNR lists winter plowing for Rockport. Its rugged quarry landscape and Besser Natural Area have different trail and parking approaches; the current registry does not establish a verified night-observing parking lot. Check the official park map and roads.

places.name: Thompson's Harbor State Park
places.note: State preserve; Michigan DNR lists winter plowing, but conditions are not verified live.
places.intro: A remote Lake Huron shoreline park with protected nighttime darkness.
places.whatToWatch: Wetlands, shoreline hazards and remote trails make route choice important after dark.
places.access: Michigan DNR currently lists winter plowing; verify actual access and local conditions.

arrival.arrival: Michigan DNR explicitly lists winter plowing at Thompson's Harbor, but the park is remote and undeveloped; no individual overnight parking lot has been verified. Follow posted park access and check local conditions before arrival.

places.name: Wilderness State Park
places.note: State preserve; no winter plowing except near park headquarters.
places.intro: A large northern Lower Peninsula park near the Straits of Mackinac.
places.whatToWatch: Lake-effect clouds can shift over short distances and obscure the broad sky.
places.access: Michigan DNR reports no general winter plowing, except the area near headquarters.

arrival.arrival: Michigan DNR says Wilderness State Park is NOT generally plowed during winter except near park headquarters. An observing area elsewhere in the park is not automatically reachable. Confirm the actual open parking area and route.

places.name: Newport State Park
places.note: Door County wilderness park; verify after-hours access before traveling.
places.intro: Wisconsin’s wilderness state park on Door Peninsula, removed from large city light domes.
places.whatToWatch: Lake Michigan cloud bands, rough trails and darkness make current park guidance essential.
places.access: Review Wisconsin DNR trail, parking and park-entry rules; the pin is not a selected observing site.

places.name: Voyageurs National Park
places.note: Large water-based park; pin is a regional reference, not a boat access point.
places.intro: A water-oriented northern Minnesota national park under protected dark skies.
places.whatToWatch: Water access and frozen-water travel are not evaluated by this planner; do not navigate based on a sky score.
places.access: Check NPS access, night programs, roads and seasonal water conditions before planning.

places.name: Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness
places.note: Protected wilderness; permit and entry-point planning required.
places.intro: International Dark Sky Sanctuary encompassing a large protected canoe wilderness.
places.whatToWatch: Dark-sky suitability does not resolve permits, wilderness travel, navigation, storms or nighttime safety.
places.access: Select an actual legal entry point and appropriate permit; the pin is an approximate region.

places.name: Middle Fork River Forest Preserve
places.note: Champaign County preserve; check campground or astronomy program access.
places.intro: Central Illinois forest preserve devoted to conserving naturally dark nights.
places.whatToWatch: Campground and astronomy access can have distinct hours and booking rules.
places.access: Check the Champaign County Forest Preserve District event and entry guidance.

places.name: Geauga Observatory Park
places.note: Observatory park; verify public night access and programs.
places.intro: Ohio observatory park centered on night-sky education and public programs.
places.whatToWatch: Astronomy sessions and nighttime admission are program-dependent.
places.access: Check Geauga Park District for event hours and rules; a clear sky does not establish open gates.

places.name: Beverly Shores
places.note: Certified community, not a designated observing park; respect private property.
places.intro: A designated Dark Sky Community at the Indiana Dunes shore, not a dedicated dark-sky park.
places.whatToWatch: The town includes residences and private property; never treat the entire community as public observing space.
places.access: Use designated public facilities and posted park rules; verify nighttime shoreline access.

places.name: Cherry Springs State Park
places.note: North-central Pennsylvania; check separate overnight astronomy-field regulations.
places.intro: Pennsylvania’s renowned astronomy state park, included as an eastern Great Lakes-region extension.
places.whatToWatch: Stargazing fields have specific lighting and camping rules distinct from general park use.
places.access: Check the Pennsylvania DCNR astronomy field and overnight viewing requirements.

places.name: Quetico Provincial Park
places.note: Canadian wilderness park; check permits, entry and camping access.
places.intro: Ontario’s vast canoe wilderness, certified as an International Dark Sky Park.
places.whatToWatch: Wilderness permits, portages, seasons and border logistics outrank any viewing forecast.
places.access: Use Ontario Parks official entry and permit information; no U.S. NWS verdict is provided.

places.name: Lake Superior Provincial Park
places.note: RASC-designated dark-sky preserve; camping and seasonal access vary.
places.intro: Ontario’s Lake Superior dark-sky preserve, with special opportunity at developed campgrounds.
places.whatToWatch: Lake-effect cloud and open-shore wind can change the experience quickly.
places.access: Official Ontario Parks material identifies the Agawa Bay area and Rabbit Blanket Lake as viewing contexts; check opening dates.

places.name: Killarney Provincial Park
places.note: RASC-designated preserve with observatory programs; check seasonal access.
places.intro: Ontario’s first provincial RASC Dark Sky Preserve, with observatory interpretation.
places.whatToWatch: The park’s terrain and seasonal access require local trip planning.
places.access: Review Ontario Parks programs, campground reservations and park operating dates.

places.name: Point Pelee National Park
places.note: Parks Canada dark-sky preserve; after-hours entry may require events.
places.intro: Parks Canada’s southern Ontario dark-sky preserve, with curated special evening access.
places.whatToWatch: The park publishes designated after-hours Dark Sky Nights; regular entry should not be assumed.
places.access: Parks Canada identifies West Beach and the Visitor Centre parking lots for vehicle-accessible observing on scheduled nights.

places.name: Bruce Peninsula National Park
places.note: Parks Canada preserve; reservations and parking restrictions can apply.
places.intro: Canadian national park on the Bruce Peninsula, designated for the protection of dark skies.
places.whatToWatch: The lake coast, reserved parking areas and seasonal operations complicate after-hours access.
places.access: Use Parks Canada parking-reservation and visitor guidance; the map reference is not a designated night viewing area.
places.weatherSource: MET Norway Locationforecast 2.0 (CC BY 4.0); compare with Environment Canada warnings

places.name: Fathom Five National Marine Park
places.note: Marine park; pin is Tobermory access region, not an offshore observing location.
places.intro: Marine dark-sky preserve in northern Lake Huron, centered on the Tobermory region.
places.whatToWatch: The preserve includes water; a location pin must never suggest an offshore lookout or safe water travel.
places.access: Check Parks Canada programs and accessible mainland areas rather than navigating to the mapped regional coordinate.

places.name: Torrance Barrens Conservation Reserve
places.note: Ontario conservation reserve; check access, environmental rules and night use.
places.intro: Ontario’s dark-sky conservation reserve in the Muskoka region.
places.whatToWatch: Crowding, roadside parking and fragile reserve habitat warrant extra care.
places.access: Verify official conservation-reserve rules and lawful parking before a night visit.
